results.title: The B200's rental price isn't the AI overcapacity tell
highlights:
- NVIDIA's B200 GPU hourly rental prices dropped 31% in June but surged 12% by September, contradicting "overbuilt" AI market fears.

- Price disparities (e.g., $3.70-$14.24/hour) reflect provider-specific factors, not silicon value, with no single "market price" for the chip.

- Key market signals show tight supply: 12-15 month GPU delivery delays, rising forward contract prices, and older chip rates increasing in 2026.

...

In late June, the hourly rental price of Nvidia's B200 GPU fell about 31% in three weeks, from a three-month high of $6.11 down to $4.22, and traders on the prediction-market platform Kalshi bet it would not get back to that high before the month was out. It was the cleanest possible version of the AI "overbuilt" fear: new capacity landing, prices collapsing, the cycle turning.

By early September the number had already turned around. The B200 spot price stood near $6.42 an hour, up about 12% over the month — and above the very peak that had triggered the panic. Older generations of the card were repricing up with it.

Here is the part the headline gets wrong. The B200 "rental price" is not the number that decides whether the AI buildout is overbuilt. It is the noisiest, most provider-dependent figure in the whole trade, and most of the time you are just watching your own index.

...

The same physical GPU — a B200 with 192GB of HBM3e memory — rented for as little as $3.70 an hour on one neocloud in June and $14.24 an hour on a hyperscaler. That roughly 3.8x spread is not a difference in the silicon. It is provider margin, whether you are forced to buy an eight-GPU node instead of a single card, spot-versus-reserved billing, and the friction of a cloud service quota. The chip is identical in both listings.

There is no single "B200 price." Silicon Data publishes one index, Ornn another, SemiAnalysis a third, and every provider posts its own list price, and they do not agree. When a story or a title points at "the B200 rental price," it is pointing at one vendor's one index's one day's number and calling it the market.

...

The signal you cannot fake is the shape of the market, and on that shape the evidence points one way.

Forward contract prices are being renegotiated sharply upward, months ahead. Baseten, an AI inference provider, reported that its cloud vendors told it in May to expect its B200 rate to jump from $2.63 to $5.10 an hour at an October renewal — a 94% increase. The honest read, though, is that its baseline was a below-market rate it had locked in, and $5.10 is a catch-up to, and still slightly under, the prevailing spot. The magnitude is real, but it is "reprice to market," not "market prices double." The meaningful fact is directional: cloud providers are quoting increases months in advance, which tells you the buyer has no bargaining power.

The more durable number is delivery. Ordering roughly 1,000 GPUs now waits 12 to 15 months. That is the constraint no price index captures, because it is the supply side telling you it physically cannot meet demand on any shorter clock.

And the tell that overcapacity people keep missing: the old chips are getting more expensive, not cheaper. H100 and A100 rental rates are repricing up in 2026. If the market were flooded with surplus compute, you would be dumping last generation's hardware at a discount. Instead, new capacity is being absorbed and the installed base is holding — the pattern of demand that outruns supply, not demand that a chip shortage accidentally satisfies.

results.title: The SAVRN Index: GPU Market Pricing in One Place
highlights:
The market for AI capacity has no exchange, no ticker and no standard unit 1. Instead, the same capacity is sold three ways. First, a landlord sells powered space by the kilowatt-month. Second, a GPU cloud sells accelerator time by the GPU-hour. Meanwhile, a model company sells the output of that same hardware by the million tokens 1. Each seller quotes in its own unit, on its own page. Moreover, each one changes the number without an announcement 1.

...

- The SAVRN Index is one place for GPU market pricing and every price change, checked every three hours against the sellers' own feeds and pages.
- It covers four markets: GPU hours, wholesale contracts and landlord rents, frontier model tokens and open model tokens, all converted to one unit.
- The same hour of H100 time runs from $1.63 on spot to $12.29 on demand, and a $128.00 rent quote becomes $261.46 over a lease term.
- A register of 113 companies, a scarcity index of 84.9 and the seven-principle SAVRN Standard sit beside the prices.
- Every figure carries its source, its unit and its check date, and the history is never deleted.

...

The GPU page holds 190 prices from 26 providers across 10 GPUs 2. Specifically, every one is converted to one GPU for one hour and shown beside the provider’s own published price 2. However, GPUs are sold in whole units, so each card also shows the server or rack price. For example, an H100 server holds 8 GPUs, and a GB300 NVL72 rack holds 72 2.

The GPU page: every GPU's typical price by the hour, the whole-unit price, and how many prices sit behind it.

On September 13, 2026, the typical H100 price was $3.99 per GPU-hour, from 61 prices 2. That is $31.92 per hour for the 8-GPU server 2. Meanwhile, the H200 was $4.50, the B200 $6.97 and the B300 $7.89 2. In addition, the GB200 NVL72 was $10.58 per GPU-hour, or $761.90 per hour for the 72-GPU rack 2. Likewise, the GB300 NVL72 was $13.31, or $958.32 per rack-hour 2. Similarly, AMD’s MI300X was $3.45, the MI325X $2.90 and the MI355X $5.60 2. Notably, Vera Rubin NVL72 has no public price on any provider’s page 2.

...

In particular, the H100 shows the spread inside a single market. For instance, the cheapest H100 hour is $1.63 at Verda on spot 2. By contrast, the priciest on-demand hour is $12.29 at Microsoft Azure 2. Specifically, of the 61 H100 prices, 37 are on demand, 15 are reserved and 9 are spot 2. In addition, 4 offers carry no published price 2. Notably, nine of the 16 GB300 offers the Index tracks show no public price at all 2.

...

The wholesale page shows what GPU owners are paid on multi-year contracts by hyperscalers, labs and enterprises 2. In addition, it shows what landlords charge for the buildings, and who sells capacity to whom 2. Specifically, it holds 5 disclosed contract rates per GPU-hour and 19 shell leases with a median of $155.60 per kW-month 2. Notably, it also holds 47 data center contracts, of which 18 disclose no rate 2.

...

The page prices the same GPU-hour at every step from owning it to listing it. The owner’s cost comes from SemiAnalysis. Its total cost of ownership is $3.57 per GPU-hour for Vera Rubin, against $1.84 for GB200 and $2.36 for GB300, in the operator ownership scenario 9. For GB200, the HIVE contract with Cohere through Bell AI Fabric pays $3.63, 2.0 times the owner’s cost 2. Meanwhile, the median list price is $10.58, 5.8 times 2. Furthermore, the highest list price is $31.10 at Microsoft Azure, 16.9 times 2. For GB300, the lowest committed price is $3.70 at Astra Intellectus 2. Wholesale contracts pay $3.96 to $3.97, whereas the highest list price is $20 at Fireworks AI, 8.5 times the owner’s cost 2.

...

Each disclosed contract is divided by its GPUs and the hours in its term. The rate is what the seller receives before its own costs. ... Specifically, that rate comes from $17.4 billion for 100,000 GB300 GPUs ... Similarly, HIVE to Cohere is $3.63, on $220 million for 2,304 GB200 GPUs over three years 2. Finally, HIVE’s Dell contracts are $3.40, on $30 million for 504 Blackwell GPUs over two years 2. By contrast, the Nscale contract with Anthropic is about $45 billion over about six years for about 460 MW 2, 12. That is $1,358.70 per kW-month 2. However, the GPU count is not disclosed, so no per GPU-hour rate is stated for it 2.

### What the tenant pays

Landlords quote base rent per kilowatt-month. However, the tenant pays more than the quote. Specifically, across the 47 leases SAVRN read, $128 of quoted Year-1 base rent becomes $261.46 per kW-month averaged over the term 2. That is 2.04 times the quote 2.

The rent that gets quoted and what the tenant pays, per critical kilowatt-month, across the 47 leases SAVRN read.

First, the build-up starts with base rent of $128 2. Second, rent increases add $30.71, from the 3 percent annual escalator in nearly every contract 2. Third, power adds $63.92, passed through at 730.5 hours times a PUE of 1.25 times $0.07 per kWh 2. In addition, taxes, insurance and maintenance add $22.40, and improvements add $16.43 from market practice rather than a filing 2. However, network, fiber and cross-connects are absent from all 47 contracts 2. Notably, the bare powered building is $3.40 to $10.60 of the $128, the rent WhiteFiber files for a Montreal shell 2. The rest, therefore, is fit-out, cooling, redundancy, capital recovery and margin 2. Consequently, a developer or landlord can see which parts of a quote are escalators, power, operating expense and improvements before a term starts.

...

## What moved

The changes page lists every price change the Index has recorded, newest first 4. Specifically, each row carries the old price, the new price, the percentage and the feed or page it came from 4. As of September 13, 2026 the Index had recorded 5 changes across its 732 tracked prices 4.

The changes record: every price move with the old price, the new price, the percentage and its source.

All five came on September 1, 2026, when Fireworks AI stepped up its on-demand GPU prices 4. For instance, GB300 went from $18 to $20 per GPU-hour, up 11.1 percent 4. Likewise, B300 went from $12 to $15, up 25 percent, and B200 from $10 to $13, up 30 percent 4. Similarly, H200 and H100 went from $7 to $8, up 14.3 percent each 4. This page is where the record of the market accumulates. Every future move appears here with its source, and the history is never deleted 4.

...

Supply tightness scored 87.9 5. Specifically, primary-market vacancy was 1.4 percent, 80.4 percent of under-construction capacity was preleased, and six months of future capacity were available, all as of June 30, 2026 5. Equipment and power lead time scored 82.7 5. Specifically, the gas turbine lead time was five years and the plant price $3,000 per kW 5. Likewise, power transformer unit cost was 77 percent above 2019 5. In addition, GE Vernova’s gas backlog with slot reservations was 116 GW, and 474 GW of large loads were seeking interconnection at ERCOT 5. Demand and price confirmation scored 82.3 5. For instance, combined 2026 hyperscaler capital expenditure guidance was $732.5 billion 5. Similarly, the H100 rental rate index was $2.64 per GPU-hour, and colocation rent growth was 8.3 percent for 3 to 10 MW requirements 5.

...

What does an H100 cost per hour?

The typical H100 on-demand price on September 13, 2026 was $3.99 per GPU-hour, the median of 37 on-demand prices. However, the cheapest was $1.63 at Verda on spot, and the priciest on demand was $12.29 at Microsoft Azure 2.

results.title: The two clocks behind every GPU rental quote – TensorCurve
highlights:
Imagine two offers for the same GPU configuration. Both say “three months” and both show a dollar-per-hour rate. One starts today; the other starts in December. These offers solve different scheduling problems. The first provides capacity for immediate work. The second is relevant to a project whose data, model or team will only be ready later.

Without an explicit start date, a comparison can mix currently usable capacity with future availability. Without a duration, it can mix a flexible rental with an obligation that continues after the workload ends. Neither error is fixed by converting every number into dollars per GPU-hour.

...

A price record should include three time fields. The observation time tells you when the offer was seen. The start date tells you when access begins. The duration tells you the contracted period of access or payment. An expiry time, if the supplier provides one, tells you how long the quote remains valid.

...

| Immediate rental | 13 Sep 2026 | 3 months | 13 Sep 2026 |

...

## Read a published commitment curve

A term curve changes contract duration while holding the product constant. A forward-start curve instead changes when access begins. The homepage uses Verda’s H100 SXM5 80GB instance with 30 CPUs and 120GB RAM. Its published on-demand base is $3.25 per hour for one GPU.

The supplier lists discounts of 2%, 3%, 4% and 8% for commitments of one, three, six and twelve months. Applying those discounts gives $3.1850, $3.1525, $3.1200 and $2.9900 per GPU-hour. TensorCurve calculates these values; the source publishes the base and discount schedule. The chart uses equal spacing for duration categories, not a continuous calendar axis.

Source checked 13 September 2026: Verda official pricing. Calculations use the published on-demand rate and reserved discounts; they are not separately quoted transaction prices.

This is one supplier’s tariff-derived commitment curve. It does not measure the global GPU market. The pricing table does not establish a region-specific offer or a guaranteed start date. Those fields remain unverified. A price for a twelve-month commitment does not tell us what a twelve-month contract beginning next December would cost.

...

Payment commitment and capacity reservation also need separate fields. A lower effective rate does not, by itself, establish that a particular machine will be ready for a particular workload on a particular day.

results.title: The first GPUIndexes observation | GPUIndexes
highlights:
## The first observation

At 04:35 UTC on Sep 13, 2026, our first H100 SXM 80 GB snapshot contained 9 eligible single-GPU offer configurations from 6 providers. The provider-floor median was $3.08 per GPU-hour, with qualifying provider floors ranging from $2.79 to $4.29.

| Provider | Lowest eligible quote | Region |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lyceum | $2.7900 / GPU-hour | Europe |
| Massed Compute | $2.8900 / GPU-hour | us-central-12 |
| Ori | $2.9000 / GPU-hour | dallas-2 |
| VERDA | $3.2500 / GPU-hour | FIN-HEL |
| RunPod | $3.4900 / GPU-hour | global |
| Lambda Labs | $4.2900 / GPU-hour | us-south-3 |

## Why the basket matters

An H100 PCIe offer is not an H100 SXM offer. A price per GPU inside an eight-GPU instance does not mean that a single GPU can be rented at that price. The initial series fixes the model, memory, instance size and pricing lane before calculating a reference.

## A reference, not a transaction

The lowest provider quote is an observed floor. The median across providers describes the middle of those floors, with equal provider weight. It does not estimate the price of a typical completed transaction, the amount of supply, or every user’s total bill.

results.title: Runpod Raises $100M: Is the Developer Cloud Exposed?
highlights:
Runpod’s $100 M raise does not expose its developer cloud; instead it strengthens the platform with lower-cost, faster GPU compute.

...

- Runpod pricing is 25% lower than AWS.
- New GPU pool speeds GenAI workloads eightfold.
- vLLM support now includes MPT-420B and Whisper-700M.
- Valuation sits at $3.5 billion after funding.

When I first tried Runpod’s developer cloud, the price tag was striking: a fresh GPU pool priced roughly 25% lower than the comparable Amazon Web Services tier. That discount translates directly into an eight-times speed boost for Generation-AI inference when I swapped a baseline public-cloud cluster for Runpod’s pods.

...

Benchmark data from February 2026 shows Runpod’s GPU compute time on GenAI inference pipelines runs ten times faster than Google Cloud’s comparable T4 spot instances, cutting costs from $0.52 per hour to $0.05 per hour per inference.

When I compared the two platforms side by side, Google’s console forced a minimum one-hour licensing commitment. Runpod, by contrast, lets developers spin up single-pod instances in seconds, which eliminates idle resource waste for experimental workloads.

Runpod advertises PCIe-zero-latency BERT inference at $0.06 per token. In my own Q3-Q4 2026 tests, the token-level latency matched Google’s reported stability figures while keeping the bill dramatically lower.

> Runpod’s per-inference cost of $0.05/hr vs Google’s $0.52/hr represents a 90% savings.

...

## developer cloud service

Runpod’s Cloud Service tier bundles network-connected GPUs with high-bandwidth NVMe storage at a flat rate, pricing each pod at $0.07 per hour, substantially lower than Google’s equivalent (≈$0.20/h).

The pay-per-session model charges $0.30 per 1-minute launch window, which stops unproductive idle times for batch jobs and enables quick startup for many concurrent tenants.

OCI (Open Container Initiative) support means Runpod devices can host images from a central registry, reducing container pull delays to sub-0.5 second latency for RT-Model demos.

| Provider | Pod Hourly Rate | Launch Window Cost | Container Pull Latency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Runpod | $0.07 | $0.30/min | 0.4 s |
| Google Cloud | $0.20 | $0.45/min | 1.2 s |
| AWS | $0.18 | $0.40/min | 1.0 s |

When I ran a batch-processing job that required 120 minutes of GPU time, Runpod’s session-based billing saved me roughly $36 compared to the hourly model used by Google.

...

Q: How does Runpod’s pricing compare to Google Cloud for GPU workloads?

A: Runpod charges $0.05 per hour per inference on GenAI pipelines, while Google Cloud’s comparable T4 spot instances cost about $0.52 per hour, delivering roughly a ten-fold cost advantage.

results.title: GPU Rental Market Update: September 13, 2026 — overfeed.news

results.title: 美股高利率風暴下的「AI算力租賃戰」：NVIDIA穩賺不賠、CoreWeave背後風險曝光 | 美股放大鏡
highlights:
最新一筆以交易為基礎的 GPU 租賃基準價顯示，NVIDIA 的 H100 SXM 每 GPU 小時租金約為 3.17 美元，而上一代的 A100 SXM4 仍能租到每小時 1.05 美元。這些數字雖然只是市場基準，而非任何單一業者的實際報價或整體機房經濟，但已足以說明關鍵：在 AI 熱潮推升算力需求的背景下，舊世代晶片並未快速「被淘汰」，反而持續在市場上找到工作，延長硬體的收益生命週期。

...

然而，算力租得出去並不代表每一個算力供應商都能賺錢。以主打 GPU 雲端與算力租賃的 CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) 為例，其暴衝成長的財報數字與殘酷的底線形成鮮明對比。CoreWeave 在 8 月公布第二季業績，營收達 25.75 億美元，調整後 EBITDA 也高達 15.10 億美元，看起來現金流相當亮眼。但同一季，公司卻仍認列 6.26 億美元的淨損，並支出 6.40 億美元的淨利息費用。

這組數字揭示了算力租賃商的結構性難題：即使租金水準受到市場青睞，設備高昂折舊、電力與機房營運成本、以及厚重的融資利息，仍可輕易吞噬大部分毛利。NVIDIA 身為芯片供應商，只要說服客戶相信硬體有長期價值，就能在售出當下鎖定利潤；但像 CoreWeave 這類營運商，必須長期在高成本結構下維持高利用率，才能把原始投資真正轉化為股東回報。
